prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid, subordinate to all reference evidence:
U+3D070. Left component is a 王-like vertical stem bearing THREE separate horizontals: bottom horizontal slightly LONGEST, top and middle shorter, all three joined by one center vertical. Do NOT draw three hanging ritual legs on left. Right component top: a central stem crowned by TWO upward diagonal prongs and TWO short outward horizontal arms; beneath these arms, left and right, TWO small U/cup-like forms each with a crossbar defining ONE small enclosed lower counter. Keep the two cups separate from the center stem. Below the cups is ONE diamond/lozenge enclosure. The top fork's stem joins its TOP vertex. In a coherent THX-type structure, a LOWER center vertical enters its BOTTOM vertex and has a FREE SHORT UPWARD TIP INSIDE the diamond, leaving a visible gap below the top vertex. This must remain ONE connected white lozenge field around that free tip, not two counters. Below the diamond, two outward sloping/curving shoulders meet the central stem. Lower right part: a left outside vertical descends past the bottom; THREE horizontal bars extend rightward from this left vertical and through the center stem, with the LOWEST bar longest. The center vertical reaches the lowest bar. This makes TWO stacked lower-left closed fields between the left and center verticals; right ends of bars project freely. Preserve the middle lozenge, both small upper cups, three lower bars and long left lower descender. Follow the attached specimens for exact relationships.
